lawyer: Mr. Ahmed Nurur Reza with Mr. Saidur Rahman, Advocates  ------- For the Petitioner.
parties: Syed Wali Mohammad Salehuddin, Administrator General, Official Trustee and Official Receiver, Government of Bangladesh ------- Petitioner.
full_judgment:
Anwarul Hoque Chowdhury, J: This application under section 11(1) of the Administrator General's Act, 1913, is for permission to sell trust properties of the estate of Rai Bihari Lal Maitra Bahadur, a Zamindar and previously a resident of the District of Barisal. 

 2. Facts leading to this application are that, late Rai Bihari Lal Maitra Bahadur, a resident of No. 155, Lower Circular Road, Calcutta, West Bengal made a will on 5.7.1931 AD in respect of the khas lands of his Zamindary situated both in East Pakistan and West Bengal and appointed the Administrator General of the then Bengal in 1931 as sole executor of his said will. 

 3. Rai Bihari Lal Maitra Bahadur died in his Calcutta house on 7.2.1933 AD. Probate being prayed and asked by the sole executor, namely, the Administrator General of Bengal, the Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Fort William in Bengal granted letters of Administration to the Administrator General of Bengal for collection, realisation and preservation of the assets belonging to the estate of the said deceased. The will by which the Administrator General of Bengal was made the sole executor provided, inter alia, that Administrator General of Bengal will take over the property and make over the property to the Official Trustees of Bengal for the purpose of carrying out the trust created by the will. He directed the trustee that after his death a sum of Tk. 700/- per month shall be paid in cash to Testator's wife, son and son's wife Niva Rani Maitra during respective terms of their natural lives for their maintenance and a sum of Tk. 4,000/- per month out of the income of the Estate, to the University of Calcutta, for advancement of female education amongst Hindu females of Bengal and the rest and residue of the trust property shall be paid to the natural born son or validly adopted son of Testator's son and if a son was not born to or is not adopted by the son of the Testator or wife of Testator's son, then the net income of the trust property shall be paid to the University of Calcutta for the advancement of education amongst the Hindu females of Bengal until such time as a son is born to or shall be adopted by the son of the Testator or wife of Testator's son Annurudha. If there is only one son, such residue shall be made over to him on completing the age of 21 years and if more sons than one, then to such sons of Annurudha, in equal shares and this shall be for the maintenance of their education, but if no son is at all born to the Testator's son or no son is adopted, the whole of the property subject to the annuities and bequests shall go to Calcutta University to be spent for the advancement of education amongst Hindu females of Bengal. 

 4. After the partition of Bengal and India in the year 1947 and the creation of Pakistan as an independent State, the Administrator General and Official Trustee, Government of East Pakistan used to manage and administer the portion of trust properties, khas lands and zamindary situated in the greater District of Barisal, though since the creation of Pakistan none of the beneficiaries as mentioned in the trust deed made any correspondence with the petitioner demanding their allowances. 

 5. In the year 1950 AD the rent receiving interest of the said trust Estate was acquired by the Government during wholesale acquisition along with excess khas land and 100 bighas of khas lands were allotted to the trust Estate under the law and it is stated that out of that 100 bighas most portion comprises barren lands and small khal. 

 It is further stated by the Administrator General on oath before this Court that the said trust Estates are scattered in different distant mouzas of several Police Stations of the District of Barguna, Perojpur and Jhalakati and it is difficult and impracticable in the present circumstances to manage this scattered barren lands and khals and sometimes the cost of realisation exceeds the amount of collection from the khas land. 

 It has been further stated that out of 100 bigas of khas lands that were allotted to the trust Estate, local people did not surrender possession of about 5 bighas of lands to the Administrate General, Official Trustee and through Court they got the same released showing kabuliyats and dakhilas alleged to be granted by the then superior landlords and there remains 75 bigas of lands including khals and of those about 30 bighas are in possession of trespassers. The petitioner tried his best to lease out the said in barga cash rent through his office employees, but none came forward to take any such settlement except 3.10 acres of lands regarding which a bainapatra has been obtained by the Administrator General from a purchaser. It has been submitted in the supplementary affidavits that the assets of the trust has at present become a property of waste and perishable nature and within a short time the existence of the trust will be extinguished and as such for better management and administration of the trust estate and to save the same from ultimate ruin, the petitioner as trustee needs Court's permission to convert the trust property into property of permanent and immediately profitable nature and character by selling the same in auction and depositing the sale price in fixed deposit. 

 28 (1) "The High Court may on application made to it give to the Administrator General any general or special directions as to any estate in his charge or in regard to any such estate." 

 Section 28 of the Administrator General's Act thus empowers the High Court to give to the Administrator General any general or special direction as to any estate in his charge and the High Court can also, on an application, give any general or special direction to the Administrator General in regard to its administration. 

 9. In the instant case the Administrator. General has been made the sole executor of the will left by the owner of the concerned Zamindari estate which was later acquisitioned. The probate was obtained by the Administrator General of Bengal before the partition of India and the Administrator General of Bengal was the sole executor of the will to manage the property as directed in the will which appears to create trust obligation giving certain direction to the sole executors to manage the property in certain specified ways. From a reading of the said direction it appears that testator directed that ultimately in the absence of any of the survivor sons, grandsons or adopted sons, the whole income of the property should be given to the University of Calcutta to be applied by the said University for advancement of education amongst the Hindu females of Bengal. In the instant case it is the specific assertion of the Administrate, General that there is none to the knowledge of the Administrator General who could be the living beneficiary under the will as none approached him since the partition of India and, therefore, the income derived from the property would be spent as desired for similar purposes of encouraging female education and that being the present position, the trust ultimately had turned into charitable trust and hence the provisions of section 92 of the Civil Procedure Code will also be applicable which specifically provides for sale of such property in case of necessity. 

 "Where in the administration or management of trust estate by the trustee there arises circumstances which it may reasonably be supposed, neither foreseen nor anticipated by the author of the trust and is unprovided for by the trust instrument and which renders it desirable and perhaps even essential in the interest of the beneficiaries that certain acts should be done by the trustee which they themselves have no power to do and to which the consent of all the beneficiaries cannot be obtained by reason of some not being sui juris and not yet in existence, the Court will exercise its general administrative jurisdiction on behalf of the parties interested sanctioning those acts being done by the trustees." 

 19. It should be mentioned that in the absence of the beneficiary of the trust instrument the ultimate residue of the income arising out of the trust and now the sale proceeds is to go to the Calcutta University for the University authorities to use it at their own discretion for the benefit of female education in Bengal. That perhaps could not be done by the Official Trustee as per direction of the trust instrument because the Calcutta University is out of Bangladesh and the trust property is also situated outside the territorial jurisdiction of West Bengal. 

 23. The Administrator General submits that after the rent receiving interest of this Estate had been acquired by the Government, the compensation money that was sanctioned against the estate and which is assessed at Taka 62,988.15 pasia now with the Deputy Commissioner. Barisal and Jhalakati, have not yet been paid and he prays for a direction upon the Deputy Commissioners, Barisal and Jhalakati for making early payment of the said com pensation. 

 24. The compensation amount of Tk. 62,980.15 pasia now claimed by the Official Trustee need be paid and the amount need be arranged and obtained from the Government at early date for payment to the Official Trustee by the authorities concerned more in view of the fact that this is a trust money and not personal. 

 25. The cost and incidental to this' application come out of the assets of the trust estate. No. further order as to costs:
